content.text:
Refactor complete. All 4 tests still green.

## Refactor Phase Summary

**Naming evaluation (first priority)** — no renames needed. `runScenario`, `basePremiumOf`, `BASE_PREMIUM_BY_ITEM_TYPE`, `PROCESSING_FEE`, and `totalBasePremium` each already state their purpose against the four passing tests. `runScenario` in particular still fits: the spec is scenario-shaped (a customer plus a list of quote/claim steps), so the name will not need to change as claim steps arrive.

**Refactoring applied** — extracted a `quote(step: QuoteStep): StepResult` function out of `runScenario`.

This is a Rule 2 (reveals intent) improvement. Before, `runScenario` mixed two altitudes in one body: the scenario-level concern (unpack the steps, collect results) and the pricing-level concern (sum base premiums, add the fee). Now `runScenario` reads as a one-line statement of what a scenario *is* — a list of steps mapped to results — while the arithmetic lives behind a name that says what it computes.

**Rule 3 (no duplication)** — none present; the single reduce is the only pricing logic so far.

**Rule 4 (fewest elements)** — the extraction adds one element, so it works against this rule in isolation. It is justified because Rule 2 outranks Rule 4, and because the extraction creates the seam the remaining spec clearly needs: 40 pending tests, of which roughly half are premium modifiers (curse surcharge, enchantment surcharge, loyalty discount, rounding) that all belong inside `quote`, while the claim tests need a sibling `claim` handler that `runScenario` will dispatch to. The alternative — letting `runScenario` accumulate all of that inline — would have to be undone within a few cycles.

**APP mass**

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Constants | 2 (`0` seed, `0` index) | 2 |
| Bindings | 5 (`scenario`, `items`, `total`, `item`, `totalBasePremium`) | 5 (`items` destructured, `total`, `item`, `totalBasePremium`, `scenario`) |
| Invocations | 8 (`reduce`, `basePremiumOf`, two `+`) | 10 (adds the `quote` call) |
| Conditionals / Loops / Assignments | 0 | 0 |
| **Total** | **15** | **17** |

Mass rose by 2, entirely from the new `quote` invocation. I accepted the increase deliberately: Rule 2 trumps APP, and mass is a tiebreaker between designs of equal clarity, not a target to minimize on its own. Paying 2 mass to separate the scenario-dispatch concern from the pricing concern is the right trade here.

One thing worth flagging for the next cycles: `basePremiumOf` returns `undefined` for an unrecognized item type, and TypeScript's `Record<string, number>` does not catch it. That currently surfaces as a `NaN` premium rather than an error. I left it alone because no test demands it yet — the pending test `"rejects a quote containing an item with an unknown type"` is the one that will force the fix, and implementing it now would be running ahead of the tests.
